column4: Visit note | 2026-09-08 03:00 PM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Kanai Roy, 36, male. Mr. Roy returns for a review visit reporting that both of his eyes are severely affected, remaining constantly itchy, watery, and red. He notes that the discomfort has been ongoing and bothersome throughout the day, interfering with his daily tasks. He works as a beautician, and this flare-up started during the flowering season in Kushtia when exposure to pollens and dust was higher at his salon. He mentions that splashing cold water temporarily relieves the itch, but the redness quickly returns. He denies any sharp eye pain, sudden flashes of light, new dark floaters, or severe loss of central vision, though he admits mild blurriness when his eyes tear excessively. He has no known chronic systemic conditions like diabetes or hypertension, and he takes no regular medications. On examination, his visual acuity 6/12 in the left eye, while the right eye tests similarly with mild mucoid discharge present. There is noticeable bilateral conjunctival hyperemia and papillary reaction on the upper tarsal conjunctiva, but the corneas remain clear with no fluorescein staining. Other vitals taken during the consultation are BP 128/76 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, and weight 61 kg. Assessment: Allergic conjunctivitis. Plan: a prescription was issued for eye drops and supportive care. He was counselled at length regarding his condition and advised to avoid rubbing the eyes at all costs, use cool compresses several times a day to soothe irritation, and wear sunglasses outdoors to block wind and pollen. Follow-up is scheduled in 2 weeks to reassess conjunctival inflammation and visual comfort.
